name: Jeffrey Hessekiel
current_role: EVP, Chief Legal & Administrative Officer, Cytokinetics (since Nov 2025)
profile: Biopharma lawyer who was EVP & General Counsel of Exelixis from 2014 to 2025, leading 100+ legal, IP, compliance, quality and government-affairs staff. Earlier he spent a decade at Gilead (ending as Chief Compliance & Quality Officer) and was Senior Counsel at Arnold & Porter. In November 2025 he joined Cytokinetics as EVP, Chief Legal & Administrative Officer.
interesting_fact: Before law school he worked with international nongovernmental organizations; he went on to hold legal roles at Wilson Sonsini and Heller Ehrman before moving in-house at Gilead in 2002.
deep_cut_fact: He serves on the board of HairToStay, a nonprofit that helps cancer patients afford scalp cooling to preserve their hair during chemotherapy, as well as Biocom California and Life Sciences Cares. Duke political science BA; GWU Law JD.
notes: Corporate executive, not a founder; low public profile. Cytokinetics media/IR contact in 2026 releases is Diane Weiser, SVP Corporate Affairs (company line published in releases, e.g. https://ir.cytokinetics.com/press-releases/press-release-details/2026/Cytokinetics-to-Participate-in-June-Investor-Conferences/default.aspx).

name: L Reade Fahs
current_role: Executive Chairman, National Vision Holdings (America's Best, Eyeglass World)
profile: Optical-retail veteran who led National Vision as CEO for 23 years (2002 to Aug 2025), building the discount eyewear chain behind America's Best and Eyeglass World and taking it public in 2017. Before that he spent a decade at LensCrafters and ran Vision Express in the UK. Since August 2025 he has been Executive Chairman, with Alex Wilkes as CEO.
interesting_fact: He chaired VisionSpring for a decade and has sat on RestoringVision's board for ~20 years; the company says the two nonprofits have provided eyeglasses to over 30 million low-income people worldwide during his tenure.
deep_cut_fact: Between LensCrafters/Vision Express and National Vision he was CEO of First Tuesday, the European dot-com era internet start-up/network. He started at LensCrafters in 1986 in advertising and new product development, and holds a Harvard BA in English and American Literature.
notes: Also on boards of PetVet Care Centers (KKR), Atlanta Committee for Progress and Alliance Theatre; active with the Coalition for Clear Vision. Emails taken from release boilerplate (could not re-fetch page directly).

name: Richard Scott Struthers
current_role: Co-founder and CEO of Crinetics Pharmaceuticals (acquired by Vertex, Sept 2026); Chairman, Radionetics Oncology
profile: Endocrinologist-turned-founder (PhD, UC San Diego) who co-founded Crinetics in 2008 after a decade at Neurocrine, and built it into the maker of Palsonify (paltusotine), an FDA-approved oral acromegaly drug. Vertex agreed to buy Crinetics for ~$10B ($85/share) in July 2026, its largest-ever deal, closing Sept 1, 2026. His post-close role was not found.
interesting_fact: The Vertex deal (about $10B, roughly a 100% premium) was the largest acquisition in Vertex's history, and paid out a company Struthers co-founded with three fellow scientists in 2008.
deep_cut_fact: Long before Crinetics he co-founded ScienceMedia, an e-learning company for the life sciences and higher-ed markets, and did his doctoral research at the Salk Institute. At Neurocrine he launched the oral non-peptide GnRH antagonist program that produced elagolix. He was elected to the BIO board in March 2026.
notes: Crinetics is now a Vertex company; corporate press routes likely via Vertex media relations. Also co-founded the San Diego Entrepreneurs Exchange (nonprofit for early-stage startups) - good angle for an entrepreneurship podcast. Post-acquisition title unconfirmed.

name: Alexandre Weinstein Manieu
current_role: Chairman of the Board and ~30% shareholder, Pluri Inc. (Nasdaq/TASE: PLUR); President, Sofgen Pharma (formerly Procaps Group)
profile: Chilean pharma entrepreneur (usually spelled Alejandro Esteban Weinstein Manieu) who ran CFR Pharmaceuticals as CEO from 2000 to 2014, expanding it to 26 countries before its US$3.3B sale to Abbott. Now Switzerland-based, he invests in health/biotech: he put US$6.5M into Israeli cell-technology firm Pluri in 2025 and became its chairman in Dec 2025, and regained control of Procaps (now Sofgen Pharma) in 2024.
interesting_fact: He built CFR from a local Chilean drugmaker into a family pharma group present in 26 countries on three continents, which Abbott bought for about US$3.3 billion.
deep_cut_fact: He has been a board member of Project Blue, an effort to build a small space telescope to directly image an Earth-like planet around Alpha Centauri, and was an International Council member of Harvard's Belfer Center. He also helped set up Chilean stem-cell banks Vidacel and Banco de Vida.
notes: Input name 'Alexandre' is a variant; he is Alejandro Weinstein. Low public/social-media profile; best route is via Pluri IR or Sofgen. Lives in Switzerland and is a GP at PE/VC firms investing in US, Israel and Europe (per Belfer bio). Web search quota ran out mid-research; Pluri press email not verified.
